summary: A is preferable because the production changes are effectively identical, while A preserves the existing Add test and adds retry coverage instead of replacing and weakening it.
reasons: A retains TestFilesService_Add, preserving its successful-request and response assertions; B replaces that test and drops the Add-specific Name assertion.
A adds separate retry tests for both caller-encoded Add bodies and Upload multipart bodies, including verification that every retry receives identical content.
A’s Upload retry test verifies the required multipart field name, uploaded filename, and content on both attempts.
A adds useful API documentation directly on Add and Upload with the buffering/retry behavior.
risks_a: Upload calls the new private add helper rather than FilesService.Add, contrary to the explicit contract requiring routing through Add.
No added tests cover empty filenames, nil content, or source-reader failures.
Changing Add to eagerly read the entire body may alter timing and memory behavior beyond the stated convenience API, though it addresses replayability.
risks_b: Upload bypasses FilesService.Add through the same private add helper, violating the required reuse path.
It removes the existing Add test, conflicting with the instruction not to weaken existing tests and reducing direct success-path coverage.
No added tests cover empty filenames, nil content, or source-reader failures.
